title: Routine-data machine learning predicts liver metastasis at pancreatic cancer diagnosis
summary: The LiMPC model, an extreme gradient boosting classifier on 21 routine clinical variables, was developed in 2657 patients from one tertiary center. In external validation across five hospitals (n = 272) it reached AUROC 0.78, sensitivity 0.81 and specificity 0.55, with CA19-9, CEA, GGT and age as key predictors by SHAP. Discrimination is moderate, specificity is low, and the study is retrospective.
ai_technology: LiMPC, an extreme gradient boosting model with isotonic calibration and SHAP interpretation

evidence.tested: Development in 2657 patients from one center and external validation in five hospitals (n = 272).
evidence.unknown: Prospective and clinical utility; the authors' supplementary analyses were not fully visible; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Predicts liver metastasis at diagnosis from routine laboratory and clinical data.
